newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium to be in first EMU group - Dehaene.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to be in first EMU group - Dehaene.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Monday there was no doubt that his country would be in the first group of European Union nations to take part in the single currency.

"There is no doubt that Belgium, because of efforts already made and respect for budgetary targets in the course in 1997, will be part of the first group of countries," Dehaene said in the text of a speech to be delivered at the first meeting of the General Commission on the Euro at Belgium's central bank.

"At the coming budget control we will ensure that we reach that target and take additional austerity measures if necessary. Belgium will respect the Maastricht Treaty criteria in letter as well as in spirit," he said.
He added that the stability of the Belgian franc against the mark and its strong trade surplus should remove any last doubts.
Belgium's 1997 budget plans to cut the state deficit to 3.0 percent of gross domestic product.
The government's annual review, at which it ensures that the budget remains on track, is due to be completed by mid-March.
European Union nations will decide early next year which countries qualify to join the single currency in January 1999.
